authors: Shinichiro Shirota
title: Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data (v1 title; OpenAlex and a later web listing show the title 'Conditional validity of prediction-powered inference for spatially dependent finite populations', so the title was probably changed in a later version)
full_text_open: yes (abstract and HTML readable; the PDF fetch returned empty text; the HTML summary I received looked truncated)
what_it_holds: v1: design-based PPI for a fixed finite population of grid cells (N=48,175 in simulation, Estonian LUCAS land cover in application); estimand is the census mean, randomness only from the labelling mechanism. Labels drawn by simple, stratified or spatially balanced (blocked, GRTS, local pivotal) designs of units, not whole clusters, as far as the text I saw shows. Selection may depend on the map and map-derived uncertainty with propensities estimated; sandwich inference and a double-robustness result are given, plus a remainder that does not shrink as labels grow under spatially coherent residuals (so conditional coverage can worsen). Exact design variances for SRS and stratified; Horvitz-Thompson and Hajek forms; normal reference, no t, no small-sample correction, and no explicit finite-population correction seen. The later-version abstract (OpenAlex) speaks of finite-population regression coefficients, nonuniform label acquisition and a spectral-basis coverage theorem; I could not confirm what changed between versions.

authors: David Broska; Michael Howes
title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference (already recorded; new details only)
full_text_open: yes (HTML read, but the text I received stopped inside Section 2.3)
what_it_holds: New details from the HTML. Superpopulation model with iid clusters and arbitrary within-cluster dependence; random cluster size; estimand is the unit-level ratio E[sum Y]/E[m_g]. Labelling is Bernoulli(p_g) at the unit level, so clusters can be fully, partly or not labelled; whole-cluster versus partial labelling is only a design remark in the introduction. Variance is a closed-form cluster sandwich with divisor G and normal intervals; I saw no n-1 divisor, t reference, CR2, or finite-population treatment in the portion I read. Simulation and application cluster counts were not in the text I saw. OpenAlex lists 0 citing works.

authors: Jyotishka Datta; Nicholas G. Polson
title: Prediction-Powered Inference with Inverse Probability Weighting
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Shows the PPI correction has a design-based survey sampling interpretation and handles unequal labelling probabilities with Horvitz-Thompson and Hajek weighting, with known or estimated inclusion probabilities (estimated from a correctly specified model). Simulations show estimated-probability IPW-PPI behaves like the known-probability version with nominal coverage. Abstract does not mention clusters, finite-population correction, cross-fitting variance or t intervals.

authors: Ziming An; Mehdi Dagdoug; David Haziza; Yves Tillé
title: Agnostic Model-Assisted Estimation with Machine Learning for Survey Data
full_text_open: yes (HTML summary read; PDF fetch empty)
what_it_holds: Design-based, finite-population framework for model-assisted estimation with any ML learner and general designs given by inclusion probabilities (Bernoulli, SRSWOR, Poisson, conditional Poisson; stratified SRSWOR in an appendix). Treats design-aware and design-agnostic cross-fitting, exact design-unbiasedness under conditions, design consistency, asymptotic normality, consistent variance estimation from cross-fitted residuals, and the Godambe-Joshi bound. I found no cluster or multistage design, no finite-population correction statement, no t reference, and no simulation sizes in the text I received. Dated after 1 September 2026.

authors: Stephen Salerno; Zhenke Wu; Tyler McCormick
title: Spatially Robust Inference with Predicted and Missing at Random Labels
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Labels missing at random with spatial dependence including clustered sampling. Doubly robust estimator with cross-fit nuisance functions; shows cross-fitting induces fold-level correlation that distorts spatial variance estimators, and proposes a jackknife spatial HAC variance. Asymptotically valid intervals; finite-sample calibration improves in simulations, largest under MAR labelling and clustered sampling. Superpopulation framing; number of clusters not seen.

authors: Shahzar Rizvi; David Burt; Vishwak Srinivasan; Renato Berlinghieri; Stefano Del Col; Tamara Broderick
title: Prediction-powered inference for time series across space
what_it_holds: Each location gets its own interval from a short labelled series, a longer unlabelled covariate series and a pooled predictor. Variance is Newey-West HAC applied to predictions and to residuals; intervals use z quantiles. No spatial clustering, no small-sample correction, no design-based treatment; simulation on 121 locations with thousands of time points. Dated after 1 September 2026, before 13 October 2026.

authors: Virginia L. Ma; Emmanuel J. Candès
title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL
venue_or_arxiv: arXiv:2606.03211 (month from the id; the page I read gave no date)
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Builds on active statistical inference: learns a smooth labelling policy from a model's uncertainty scores to minimise estimator variance, then does inference on the labelled units. Uses a histopathology example (breast cancer subtype, odds ratios across demographic groups). Unit-level labelling; abstract does not mention clusters, finite populations or small-sample corrections.

authors: Adam Fisch; Joshua Maynez; R. Alex Hofer; Bhuwan Dhingra; Amir Globerson; William W. Cohen
title: Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference for Hybrid Language Model Evaluation
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] PPI with stratified sampling of labelled units, with intervals valid for population averages and narrower with good strata and allocation. Superpopulation language evaluation setting; no cluster labelling or small-sample correction mentioned.

authors: Riccardo Fogliato; Pratik Patil; Mathew Monfort; Pietro Perona
title: A Framework for Efficient Model Evaluation through Stratification, Sampling, and Estimation
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Stratifies items by predicted model performance (k-means), samples labels within strata and uses model-assisted estimators with predictions on the unlabelled part. Gains about tenfold over simple random sampling on vision datasets. Prediction-guided stratified selection of units, not clusters.

authors: Tijana Zrnic; Emmanuel J. Candès
title: Cross-Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Cross-fitted PPI that imputes labels with models trained on folds of the labelled data and debiases; more powerful and more stable than PPI that holds out labelled data to train. iid labelled and unlabelled data; no clusters.

authors: Se Yoon Lee; Jae Kwang Kim
title: Statistical Optimality of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] M-estimation view of PPI under simple random sampling without replacement, with efficiency bound, cross-fitting theory and a single-fit variant with a variance correction. Survey-statistics authorship but no clusters mentioned.

authors: Pranav Mani; Peng Xu; Zachary C. Lipton; Michael Oberst
title: No Free Lunch: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Exact finite-sample analysis of PPI++ for mean estimation under sample splitting; PPI++ beats labels-only inference only when correlation exceeds a threshold depending on n (about 1/sqrt(n-2) in the Gaussian case). Relevant to very few labelled units, not to clusters.

authors: Benjamin Eyre; David Madras
title: Regression for the Mean: Auto-Evaluation and Inference with Few Labels through Post-hoc Regression
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] PPI++ can be worse than labels-only inference when real labels are scarce; links PPI++ to OLS and proposes robust-regression variants for the few-label regime. iid units; no clusters.

authors: Yiqun T. Chen; Moran Guo; Shengyi Li
title: Power Analysis for Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Closed-form power and sample-size formulas for PPI (two-sample, paired, 2x2 risk measures); labelled sample savings roughly proportional to R squared. Examples include single-cell transcriptomics. iid units.

authors: Reagan Mozer (already recorded; no new reading)
title: PPI is the Difference Estimator
what_it_holds: Abstract only re-read. States PPI mean estimator equals the Cassel et al. 1976 difference estimator and PPI++ equals GREG; notes differences in mode of inference. Nothing found on clusters.

authors: Taekwon Hong; Daeyoung Lim; Woojung Bae
title: Beyond Point Estimates: Reliable Evaluation of Prediction Performance Metrics under Clustered Data
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Cluster-robust sandwich intervals for accuracy, F1 and similar metrics under clustered data, with power approximations. Not PPI; no predictions-for-unlabelled-units component.

authors: Shuichi Nishino; Tomohiro Shiraishi; Teruyuki Katsuoka; Ichiro Takeuchi
title: Post-ADC Inference: Valid Inference After Active Data Collection
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Selective-inference approach for valid inference after adaptive, model-driven data collection (black-box optimisation). Different route to the C0 problem (conditioning rather than inclusion probabilities); not PPI and not clustered.

authors: Dan M. Kluger; Stephen Bates
title: M-estimation under Two-Phase Multiwave Sampling with Applications to Prediction-Powered Inference (already recorded; new note only)
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Adaptive multiwave choice of which units to measure with proxies for all units; asymptotic normality. Unit-level; no clusters seen. Listed only because the arXiv number in the brief is confirmed correct.

authors: (authors not read)
title: A Note on the Prediction-Powered Bootstrap
what_it_holds: [from title and listing only] A bootstrap for PPI. Possibly relevant as an alternative to t-based small-sample intervals; I did not read it.

authors: Soham Mallick; Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen; Edgar Dobriban; Yonghoon Lee
title: Generalized Hierarchical Conformal Prediction
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Conformal prediction sets for a new observation from an unseen group under hierarchical exchangeability, using a few observations from the test group; illustrated on American Community Survey data. Prediction sets, not PPI intervals. Dated mid-August 2026.
